meta.title: Move the platform team to a one-week on-call rotation in January

slides.title: Move the platform team to a one-week on-call rotation in January
body: Response to pages slows by more than half in the second week of a two-week shift. Halving the shift keeps everyone in the fast first week, costs no new hire, and can be reversed at any handover.

slides.title: Approve a one-week on-call shift for the six platform engineers
body: Starting Monday 5 January, with a review on 30 March.
Why now: median time to acknowledge a page rises from 4.3 minutes in week one to 7.5 in week two, and two of six engineers have asked to leave the rotation.
Cost: no new hire. Each engineer is on call the same number of days a year, in shorter stretches, with twice as many handovers (52 a year instead of 26).
Stop if: any handover drops an open incident, or week-one response is no faster by the March review.
sources: Paging system export, 1 July to 30 September 2026; Platform team survey, September 2026; team roster and rotation schedule, October 2026; recruiting records for the last two platform hires, 2025 and 2026

slides.title: Six engineers share a two-week shift that pages about four times a night
body: Each engineer holds the pager for fourteen days, then hands over to the next. Pages arrive mostly at night, when batch jobs run. The figures come from the paging system export for July to September.
The rotation is now losing people.

stats.label: Engineers who asked to leave the rotation

slides.title: Response time tracks days on shift, so a shorter shift is faster
body: Week one is flat at about four minutes; week two climbs every day.
The paging export shows how long each page waited before someone acknowledged it. Grouped by the day of the shift, the wait is flat through week one and climbs every day of week two.
sources: Paging export, July to September 2026, 1,046 pages.

chart.title: Median minutes to acknowledge a page, by day of shift
chart.alt: Days 1 to 7: 4.1, 4.0, 4.3, 4.2, 4.6, 4.4 and 4.8 minutes. Days 8 to 14: 5.9, 6.4, 6.8, 7.5, 7.9, 8.6 and 9.2 minutes. Week one is flat; week two rises every day.
chart.takeaway: Week one is flat at about four minutes; week two climbs every day.

slides.title: A one-week shift beats both a new hire and doing nothing
body: Hiring helps the load but not the second week, and it lands after the people asking to leave have decided. Doing nothing keeps response near five and a half minutes only while all six stay on the rotation.
sources: Response estimates use the week-one medians in figure 1 on the page; today's figure is the median of all fourteen daily medians. Days on call assume 365 days shared by the engineers on the rotation. Hiring time is from the last two platform hires.

slides.title: The switch takes three steps and ends with a review in March

steps.title: Publish the new schedule (platform lead, by 1 December)
steps.text: One-week shifts from Monday 5 January, handover Mondays at 10:00, each engineer's weeks named a quarter ahead.

steps.title: Write the handover checklist (on-call owner, by 15 December)
steps.text: Open incidents, silenced alerts, risky changes planned for the week. The checklist is the handover; nothing is passed on by memory.

steps.title: Review the first twelve weeks (platform lead, 30 March)
steps.text: Compare response by day of shift with figure 1 on the page, count dropped handovers, and ask the team again. Keep, adjust or revert using the stop conditions.

slides.title: Two failures would send us back to two weeks
body: The written checklist guards against context lost at the extra handovers. The March review also tests the other explanation, harder incidents late in the month, by comparing day of shift with day of month.
sources: Paging system export, 1 July to 30 September 2026; Platform team survey, September 2026; team roster and rotation schedule, October 2026; recruiting records for the last two platform hires, 2025 and 2026

callout.label: Stop conditions
callout.text: Revert at the next handover if any handover drops an open incident, or if week-one median response is not below 5 minutes by the March review.
